name: Bloom Filters, Counting Bloom & Cuckoo Filters
tagline: Space-optimal probabilistic set membership: zero false negatives, tunable false positives, and deletion trade-offs via Cuckoo fingerprinting.
purpose: Choose and size Bloom, Counting Bloom, and Cuckoo filters for SSTable point lookups, cache-penetration shields, and dynamic blocklists.

spark.summary: Bloom filters answer set membership in O(k) bit probes using ~10 bits per key at a 1% false-positive rate with zero false negatives, while Cuckoo filters store compact fingerprints in 2-choice hash buckets to support safe item deletion and better CPU cache locality.
spark.keyTakeaway: Never delete from a standard Bloom filter (it clears bits shared by other keys); use a Cuckoo filter when items must be removed dynamically or when low false-positive rates (<3%) need tighter memory.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** A **Bloom Filter** hashes key `x` with `k` functions into a bit array (`0` bit = definitely absent; all `1`s = probably present with false-positive rate `p`). Standard Bloom filters cannot delete items. **Cuckoo Filters** store short `f`-bit fingerprints in two candidate buckets (`b1 = h1(x)`, `b2 = b1 XOR h(fp)`), supporting deletion and eviction swaps.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Contrasts a `Bloom Filter (No Delete)` (`x` -> `h1, h2, h3` -> bit array `[0|1|0|1|1|0|1]`) against a `Cuckoo Filter (Supports Delete)` (`2-choice hash buckets` `b1, b2` holding `[fp]` fingerprints with `Evict & Kick Swap`).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** At `1%` false-positive rate, a Bloom filter uses ~9.6 bits/key, whereas a Counting Bloom filter uses 4x memory (`4-bit` counters) and risks counter overflow. Cuckoo filters use ~12.6 bits/key (or less at `<3%` FP) with 2 cache-line reads instead of `k` random probes.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Never exceed a Cuckoo filter's ~95% load factor (eviction loops fail inserts) and never delete a non-existent key from a Cuckoo filter if duplicate inserts are possible.

learningJourney.title: How Bloom Filters & Cuckoo Filters Work
learningJourney.purpose: The mechanism: understand bitset probing in Bloom filters vs. XOR-linked fingerprint buckets in Cuckoo filters.
learningJourney.explanation:
A **Bloom Filter** allocates `m` bits and `k` independent hash functions. Inserting `x` sets bits `h_1(x)...h_k(x)` to `1`. Querying `x` returns **definitely absent** if any bit is `0`, or **probably present** if all `k` bits are `1` (false-positive rate `p`). Optimal sizing uses `m = -(n * ln(p)) / (ln(2)^2)` bits (~9.6 bits/key for `p = 1%`) and `k = (m/n) * ln(2)` (~7 probes).

A **Cuckoo Filter** replaces the bitset with buckets of `b = 4` fingerprint slots. Each key `x` yields an `f`-bit fingerprint `fp` and two candidate buckets: `b1 = hash(x)` and `b2 = b1 XOR hash(fp)`. Notice `b1` can be computed from `b2` using only `fp` (`b1 = b2 XOR hash(fp)`), allowing items to be **relocated** when a bucket fills and **deleted** by removing one matching `fp`.

sectionDiagram.title: Two-Choice Cuckoo Bucket Lookup & Eviction

cards.label: Zero False Negatives
cards.detail: If neither b1 nor b2 holds fp, key x is guaranteed absent.

cards.label: Cache Locality
cards.detail: Checks at most 2 buckets (2 cache lines) vs. k=7..10 random bit probes.

cards.label: Safe Deletion
cards.detail: Removes 1 matching fp from b1 or b2 without affecting other keys.

sectionDiagram.summary: Caption: Cuckoo filters use partial-key cuckoo hashing (b2 = b1 XOR h(fp)) to relocate and delete items using only the stored fingerprint.

learningJourney.title: Why You Cannot Delete From a Standard Bloom Filter
learningJourney.purpose: The problem: see how clearing a bit in a Bloom filter corrupts unrelated keys and creates false negatives.
learningJourney.explanation: Because multiple keys hash onto overlapping bit positions, clearing a `1` bit to `0` when deleting `key_A` can silently break `key_B`—violating the **zero false negatives** invariant. Meanwhile, **Counting Bloom Filters** replace each bit with a 4-bit counter (4x RAM overhead) and suffer counter overflow if a hot key is inserted repeatedly.

ideas.title: Cache Penetration Shield
ideas.description: Checking a filter in RAM before querying Disk/Redis rejects non-existent IDs (e.g., crawler 404 storms) in nanoseconds.

ideas.title: LSM-Tree SSTable Skip
ideas.description: RocksDB/Cassandra attach per-SSTable Bloom filters so point lookups skip 99% of disk SSTables that do not contain the key.

learningJourney.title: Where Bloom vs. Cuckoo Filters Fit Best
learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: match immutable SSTables to Bloom filters and mutable blocklists/caches to Cuckoo filters.
learningJourney.explanation: Use **standard Bloom filters** for **immutable** datasets such as RocksDB/LevelDB SSTable blocks or daily batch snapshots. Use **Cuckoo filters** for **mutable** sets (session revocation lists, CDN one-hit-wonder admission caches, or active feature-flag memberships) where entries are frequently added and removed.

learningJourney.title: Sizing Bits-per-Key, Load Factor & Rebuild Thresholds
learningJourney.purpose: Operational control: bound Cuckoo load factor below 95% and guard against insertion failure.
learningJourney.explanation: Size Bloom filters with explicit `(n, p)` budgets (`~10 bits/key` for `1%` FP, `~14.4 bits/key` for `0.1%` FP). For Cuckoo filters, cap occupancy at **90–95%** (`bucket_size = 4`) and bound eviction loops (`max_kicks = 500`); if an insert exhausts `max_kicks`, trigger an asynchronous double-capacity rebuild.
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```python
import math

def bloom_sizing(expected_items: int, fp_rate: float) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Return (num_bits, num_hashes) for target expected_items and false-positive rate."""
    if expected_items <= 0 or not (0 < fp_rate < 1):
        raise ValueError("expected_items must be > 0 and 0 < fp_rate < 1")
    m = int(math.ceil(-(expected_items * math.log(fp_rate)) / (math.log(2) ** 2)))
    k = max(1, int(round((m / expected_items) * math.log(2))))
    return m, k
```

learningJourney.title: Bloom vs. Counting Bloom vs. Cuckoo vs. Ribbon Filters
learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: compare RAM per key, cache misses, deletion support, and static vs. dynamic workloads.
learningJourney.explanation: RocksDB's newer **Ribbon Filters** save ~30% RAM over Bloom filters for static immutable SSTables, while **Cuckoo Filters** win for dynamic sets needing deletion and 2-bucket cache locality.

benefits: Simple, zero resize failures, ~9.6 bits/key at 1% FP.
costs: No deletion; k=7 random bit probes cause k CPU cache misses.

benefits: Supports deletion; only 2 cache-line lookups; smaller than Bloom at <3% FP.
costs: Inserts fail above ~95% occupancy; must not delete keys that were never inserted.

learningJourney.title: Two-Stage CDN One-Hit-Wonder Filter + LSM SSTable Point Lookups
learningJourney.purpose: Production architecture: combine rotating Cuckoo filters with SSD caches to cut write amplification.
learningJourney.explanation: CDNs use a **rotating Cuckoo/Bloom admission filter** in RAM: an object is only written to NVMe SSD on its *second* request, cutting SSD write wear by 40–60% from one-hit-wonder tails while expiring old entries cleanly via filter rotation.

cards.detail: Swap active/passive filters hourly to bound false-positive saturation.

cards.detail: 2 bucket checks in L2/L3 CPU cache add <50ns overhead.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does deleting a key by clearing its bits in a standard Bloom filter break correctness?

options.text: Other inserted keys may share those bit positions, so clearing them introduces false negatives
options.feedback: Correct: Bloom filters forbid deletion because multiple keys map to overlapping bits.

options.text: Clearing bits doubles the false-positive rate immediately
options.feedback: Incorrect: clearing bits causes false negatives, not false positives.

options.text: Bloom filters only store 1 bit total
options.feedback: Incorrect: Bloom filters use m bits across k hash probes.

knowledgeChecks.question: How does a Cuckoo filter compute a key's alternate bucket b2 during eviction without storing the original key?

options.text: Using partial-key cuckoo hashing: b2 = b1 XOR hash(fp)
options.feedback: Correct: XOR is self-inverse, so b1 and b2 can always be derived from each other using only the compact fingerprint fp.

options.text: By querying the backing PostgreSQL database on every kick
options.feedback: Incorrect: Cuckoo filters stay 100% in memory with zero DB lookups.
Incorrect: lookup and relocation are O(1) across exactly two candidate buckets.

knowledgeChecks.question: What happens if you insert into a Cuckoo filter that is >95% full?

options.text: Eviction kick chains can cycle and hit max_kicks, requiring a resize/rebuild
options.feedback: Correct: Cuckoo filters degrade sharply above ~95% occupancy and must be sized with headroom.

options.text: It silently converts into a B-Tree
options.feedback: Incorrect: it fails insertion once max_kicks is reached.

options.text: False negatives start occurring for existing keys
options.feedback: Incorrect: existing keys remain intact; new inserts fail until resized.
